bump_pitch_um.source: UCIe advanced package bump pitch 25-55 um; the UCIe-A PHY depth above is quoted at 45 um (same Hot Chips 2023 table); CoWoS-class micro-bump array over the whole die

power_bump_fraction.source: one bump in four is VDD (one VSS, two signal/spare): a common area-array allocation; the VDD-bump pitch is bump_pitch / sqrt(fraction)

bump_contact_radius_um.source: radius of the via stack under a micro-bump pad (~half the ~20 um pad)

ir_budget_fraction.source: static IR budget of the die-level grid, 5% of VDD (a common sign-off budget; the local M1-M6 grid needs its own share)

placement_utilisation.source: standard-cell area / placed area for large hardened blocks; the low end is the median utilisation of this repository's routed V4.1 blocks (small blocks routed at low density, see ledger.utilisation_evidence)

pool_operand_in.what: spine (vector unit, chaining buffers) -> the farthest tile: the operand vector of a matvec or of an attention / indexer scan (the pooled lanes live in the tiles)
pool_operand_in.exposure: latency on the operator's input edge: charged on every such node; the DAG hides it only where the node is off the critical path

pool_result_out.what: the farthest tile -> spine: partial sums / scores back into the reducer tree
pool_result_out.exposure: latency on the output edge; charged, exposed where on path

spine_reduce.what: spine lanes -> the reducer / select / HC root at the spine's centre, and the result back along the spine (half the spine's length each way)
spine_reduce.exposure: charged; the vector unit is one strip the core's height long

collective_edge.what: spine -> the one-shot engine at the UCIe / package-pair edge and back (the two levels run in parallel: the longer is charged)
collective_edge.exposure: charged: the bench-measured tails (behavioural links) contain no on-die wire

stage_hop_edge.what: the residual from the sender's spine to its SerDes edge and from the receiver's SerDes edge to its spine
stage_hop_edge.nodes: hop, wire_in (sender spine -> SerDes) + wire_out (SerDes -> receiver spine)
stage_hop_edge.exposure: charged: the RTL hop tails start and end at the link endpoints

kv_gather_request.what: the top-k indices from the select (spine) to the nearest HBM3E controller
kv_gather_request.exposure: charged: a data-dependent address exists only after the select; the rows' return PHY -> tile is shorter than the scan's operand broadcast charged on the scan (far_tile >= hbm_to_tile), so it is covered there

rom_to_lane_in_tile.what: the farthest ROM macro -> its tile's lane column (weights never leave the tile)
rom_to_lane_in_tile.exposure: HIDDEN: a static-address stream issued ahead of the activation

kv_static_rows.what: HBM3E PHY -> tiles for window rows, reuse-layer selections and index keys
kv_static_rows.exposure: HIDDEN: static addresses, prefetched one layer ahead into the staging buffers (docs/ARCH_SPEC_V41.md s6 item 4; arch_budget_v41 kv_state prefetch)

cooling_reference.note: no committed source publishes a sustainable hot-spot W/mm2 (configs/hardware/power_scenarios.json: 'none found'); the screen uses H200's published die-average flux (700 W package less its stacks over 814 mm2) as a conservative local limit: a shipping die's hottest region sustains at least its average

power.attribution: mac -> engine tiles; weight_read_and_delivery -> ROM; stream -> vector spine; kv_sram -> SRAM; links -> SerDes strip; hbm_controller_phy_io (power_scenarios' die share of HBM energy, 10.19 pJ/b: controller + PHY + I/O) -> the HBM PHY strips, the pessimistic placement; static: leakage and clock on each region's placed area plus the always-on SerDes, UCIe idle and HBM idle on their PHYs

ir_drop.model: closed form: a sheet of resistance R per square, loaded uniformly at J A/um2, fed at a square array of VDD bumps of pitch p through contacts of radius a; each bump's cell is taken as the disk of equal area (radius R = p / sqrt(pi)), which gives a drop of J R / 2 x (R^2 ln(R/a) - (R^2 - a^2)/2) from the bump to the cell edge; charged on VDD and VSS alike

grid.source: tools/chip_assembly/tcl/pdn_die.tcl (M8/M9 -width 1.0 -pitch 40.0, VDD and VSS each once per pitch)

ir_drop.layer_rc_source: ORFS asap7 platform setRC.tcl (set_layer_rc M8/M9; kOhm/um at 40 nm width)
ir_drop.not_modelled: the local M1-M6 grid, via stacks, the interposer and package; transient (L di/dt) droop, which the stage clock gating's wake-up makes the first-order PDN risk

clock.plan: one PLL per die from the tray reference; a global H-tree on the top metals to the 64 regions (the 48 tiles, the spine and the edge PHY regions); each region is its own balanced local tree (as the routed blocks' CTS) with an integrated clock gate at its boundary for stage clock gating; paths BETWEEN regions are the pipelined long wires of the floorplan and are timed mesochronously (a region-to-region hop re-times into the receiver's clock through a small bisynchronous FIFO, or with a per-region delay-locked skew adjust), so the global tree's skew never sits on a single-cycle path
clock.global_tree_basis: C = 0.145426 fF/um (ASAP7 set_wire_rc -clock) x length x 2.0 (repeaters), P = C V^2 f
clock.whole_die_clock_basis: power_scenarios die.clock_j_per_mm2_per_cycle on the ledger's logic and ROM areas (ROM at the 0.15 region multiplier), ungated -- the upper bound stage gating removes
clock.verdict: a single synchronous tree across the die is not viable: at the skew/insertion ratio the routed matrix engine measured, the global tree's skew alone is a large fraction of the 920 ps period; regional trees with mesochronous crossings are required (the rack already runs every link plesiochronously, results/rtl/v41_link_cdc_campaign.json)

verdict.long_wire_timing: closes with pipelining (every path is registered at the per-cycle reach); the latency is charged in the design point

area.condition: placement utilisation >= 0.68 at MTP m = 2 (ledger assumes 0.70); m = 1 or the N5 logic credit leave > 150 mm2

long_wire_timing.verdict: closes by pipelining; latency charged in the design point
long_wire_timing.condition: 21.1 us per token (ASAP7 routed-wire model; 5.6 at 150 ps/mm) in the headline; floorplan levers would recover it

power.verdict: scenario B exceeds both the air and the liquid die limit at its worst point; scenario A fails
power.condition: hottest die (power_scenarios.v41_hottest_die): B worst 531 W vs air 374.56 / liquid 474.56 W; A worst 6,538 W

ir.verdict: closes with a denser top grid
ir.condition: B hot spot 64 mV vs 35 mV on the repository's 2.5% M8/M9 grid; 4.5% coverage per net closes it

clock.verdict: closes only as regional trees with mesochronous crossings
clock.condition: a single synchronous tree across the die is not viable: at the skew/insertion ratio the routed matrix engine measured, the global tree's skew alone is a large fraction of the 920 ps period; regional trees with mesochronous crossings are required (the rack already runs every link plesiochronously, results/rtl/v41_link_cdc_campaign.json)

verdict.summary: on the adopted design point the layer die closes CONDITIONALLY: on area only above the stated placement utilisation (the MTP lane multiplier is what fills it), on power only in scenario B (and there not at every operating point: the hottest die -- the stage that holds an uncapped index scan -- exceeds even the liquid limit at its worst point), on IR only with a denser top grid than the repository's die grid, on the clock only as regional trees, and on long-wire timing only by pipelining every spine/tile/PHY traversal -- whose per-token latency the design point now charges

top_risks.detail: the layer die needs 806 mm2 at 0.70 placement utilisation (+9 mm2 of whitespace); it closes above 0.68 utilisation, or at m = 1 (+187 mm2), or with the N5 logic credit (+168 mm2); the MTP lane multiplier m = 2 is what fills the die, and 'inside the 328.9 mm2 envelope' compared standard-cell area with a placed-area envelope

the design point now charges its registered on-die traversals: 21.1 us per 1M token on the ASAP7 routed-wire model (15% of the 142.7 us token; 5.6 us on technology.json's 150 ps/mm); the 1M rate is 7,009 tok/s/user (7,828 at 150 ps/mm, 8,185 with no wire); the levers are sub-spines and collective engines at the tile rows
on the measured ASAP7 MAC energy the worst point draws 6,538 W per die against the 374.56 W air / 474.56 W liquid die limits; the engine tiles run at 22.44 W/mm2

the worst production point is 531 W per die (over the air limit, over liquid); engine tiles 1.09 W/mm2 and the hottest region (phy_hbm) 3.09 W/mm2 against the H200 die average 0.675: the PHY strips, not the engines, are the thermal hot spots

the repository's die grid (M8/M9 1 um at 40 um) on ASAP7's thin top metals drops 64 mV in the scenario-B hot spot against a 35 mV budget (needs 4.5% M8/M9 coverage per net); a production N5 stack's thick top metal and RDL change this by an order of magnitude, so it is an ASAP7 statement, not an N5 one

a single synchronous tree across the die is not viable: at the skew/insertion ratio the routed matrix engine measured, the global tree's skew alone is a large fraction of the 920 ps period; regional trees with mesochronous crossings are required (the rack already runs every link plesiochronously, results/rtl/v41_link_cdc_campaign.json)
the 112G lane area is assumed and the HBM3E PHY is an abstract; the UCIe module is the only published PHY footprint
